data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Lyssa is the goddess of madness, frenzy, and rabies. Her name derives from the Greek word 'lyssos', meaning 'loosener', due to her ability to unleash wild, untamed emotions. In Christianity, Lyssa represents the transformative power of the Holy Spirit, turning chaos into divine order. The name Lyssa carries the meaning “Goddess of the Moon” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Lyssa usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.

She represents the irrational and untamed aspects of human nature that often lie beneath the surface. The name might evoke images of fierce passion or perhaps a subtle reminder of the lurking madness in all of us.
